Keywords: Though, The, Each

outputs.L1:
Though it is all too clear how unimpressed you remain by any cri de cœur, and being left unembraced is, from your vantage, simply de rigueur for schemes to rendezvous with you—still, I remain a restless entrepreneur. The mere thought of you transforms my favorite entrées into mere hors d'oeuvres; my addiction to the tingling sensation you induce is now a fait accompli. Each drifting day adds another page to this secret book whose dénouement never arrives, while your fleeting glances bind me ever tighter to this unfinishable roman à clef.

The notion that some single remembered moment—at a party, at a picnic—was my one lost chance to touch you must surely be a cul-de-sac. Whenever my plans for a prudent career attempt to assert themselves, the memory of your voice delivers the coup de grâce, and my mélange of bright ideas dissolves into mere potpourri. How I would love to believe this dance between us is a folie à deux.

The way you stride across Memorial Drive is nothing short of a tour de force, though glimpses of you across traffic yield only a paper-thin raison d'être. Your recent departure seems foretold in every mise en scène—as if you sensed me drawing near for a tête-à-tête and slipped into the elevator, tall boots and sangfroid intact.

Always you contrive to reculer, while I never quite manage to mieux sauter. And still, I will keep watch for you on every rez-de-chaussée.

Merely picturing you transforms my beloved entrées into mere appetizers. My craving for the electric feeling you spark in me is now undeniable fact. Every passing day adds another chapter to a hidden story that refuses to conclude, while your brief looks trap me inside this endless tell-all novel. Believing that some remembered instant at a gathering was my one irretrievable shot at reaching you must surely be a dead end. Whenever my sensible career plans attempt to rise, the memory of your voice delivers the final blow, reducing my collection of clever ideas to a jumbled mess. Watching you cross Memorial Drive is a masterful display, yet catching sight of you through passing cars gives me only a flimsy purpose for existing. Your latest departure seems woven into countless staged scenes. It's almost like you sensed me coming for a private conversation and ducked into the elevator, tall boots and cool composure intact. You always get to retreat, while I never manage to leap forward— Still, I'll keep watching for you on every ground floor.
outputs.L3:
I know you feel nothing when I lay my heart bare before you. I know that every time our paths threaten to cross, you find some reason to slip away, to be elsewhere, to remain just out of reach. And still, despite this knowledge that should by now have taught me better, I cannot stop myself from wanting what you refuse to give. I keep reaching toward you, keep hoping that persistence might somehow succeed where sincerity has failed.

This wanting has become something beyond choice or reason—an obsession that colors every waking thought. Other pleasures that once brought me satisfaction now seem pale and insufficient beside the constant hum of thinking about you. I have stopped trying to explain this to myself as anything other than what it plainly is: an addiction, as undeniable and immovable as any fact of nature. I do not fight it anymore. I simply live inside it.

My mind has become a theater that replays the same brief scenes on an endless loop—a glance held a moment too long across a crowded room, a single instant at some gathering where our eyes met and something unspoken passed between us. I turn these fragments over and over, examining them from every angle, wondering if that fleeting exchange was the one chance I was given and failed to seize. The fear that this was my only opportunity, now irretrievably lost, follows me like a shadow I cannot outrun.

Even my ambitions, the practical plans I once pursued with clarity and purpose, have grown unsteady. The moment I hear your voice, even in memory, my carefully constructed ideas seem to shrink into something small and unremarkable. Whatever creative spark I possessed dims in comparison to the force of simply thinking of you. My career, my goals—the things I once believed mattered—now feel like distractions from the one thing that actually consumes me.

And yet, I see the truth of this imbalance clearly enough. You are always the one who withdraws, who steps back, who maintains distance, while I am the one who never manages to close it, who remains fixed in place, unable to advance beyond longing into anything real. The unfairness of this arrangement is not lost on me. Still, knowing all of this changes nothing in my resolve. I will keep watching for you—on every ground floor, in every doorway, in every room I enter—hoping that one day the pattern might break, even as some quieter part of me suspects it never will.
outputs.L4:
# The Unattainable Beloved: An Analysis

The poem before us is a study in longing—a portrait of infatuation so consuming that it borders on obsession. From its opening lines, the speaker establishes an atmosphere of romantic desperation, one that is heightened considerably by the deliberate and extensive use of French loanwords and phrases woven throughout the English text. This linguistic choice is far from incidental. French, long associated in English literary tradition with romance, sophistication, and a certain untouchable elegance, becomes the perfect vehicle for expressing a longing that itself feels perpetually out of reach. The very language of the poem mirrors its content: foreign, alluring, and never quite fully possessed by the speaker, just as the beloved remains foreign, alluring, and never quite possessed either.

The central relationship depicted is entirely one-sided. The object of the speaker's affection is portrayed as distant, almost ethereal—a figure glimpsed rather than known, admired rather than embraced. There is no reciprocity here, no mutual exchange of feeling. Instead, the speaker exists in a perpetual state of yearning, each stanza reinforcing the futility of the pursuit. The beloved's indifference is not merely implied but made explicit through a pattern of rejection that recurs throughout the poem. Whatever advances or hopes the speaker nurtures are systematically dashed, whether through direct refusal, circumstance, or simple inattention on the part of the desired one.

Compounding this rejection is a motif of sabotage—ambitions and plans that might have brought the speaker closer to their goal are thwarted, sometimes by external forces, sometimes seemingly by fate itself. This sense of cosmic misfortune adds a layer of tragic irony to the poem: it is not only that the beloved does not return the speaker's affections, but that the universe itself appears to conspire against any possibility of union. Encounters between the speaker and the object of desire are fleeting at best, brief moments of proximity that flare up with hope only to dissolve into nothing. These meetings, rather than providing satisfaction or closure, seem only to intensify the speaker's longing, functioning as cruel reminders of what remains just beyond reach.

What makes the poem particularly poignant—and psychologically astute—is the speaker's response to this repeated pattern of disappointment. Rather than abandoning the pursuit or reconciling themselves to the impossibility of the situation, the speaker doubles down on their devotion. There is no epiphany of self-preservation, no turn toward acceptance or moving on. Instead, the poem concludes with a resolution to continue watching, waiting, and hoping for the beloved, despite every piece of evidence suggesting the futility of such devotion.

This ending encapsulates the poem's deeper thematic concern: the self-defeating nature of unreciprocated love. The speaker's fidelity to their infatuation, admirable in its intensity, becomes simultaneously tragic in its irrationality. There is something both moving and unsettling about a devotion so absolute that it persists in the face of constant rejection and disappointment. The poem thus serves as a meditation on the psychology of obsessive longing—how such feelings can consume a person entirely, distorting their sense of hope and possibility, and trapping them in a cycle of anticipation and heartbreak from which there seems to be no escape. Through its clever use of French to underscore the theme of unattainable romance, and through its unflinching depiction of a lover who cannot let go, the poem offers a powerful exploration of the darker, more compulsive dimensions of desire.
outputs.L5:
# On Fragments and Wholes

**Though** we often search for grand unifying truths, meaning tends to arrive in fragments—a fleeting conversation, a half-remembered lesson, the quiet ache of nostalgia. We build our understanding of the world not through single revelations but through countless small moments stitched together over time. Though we crave certainty, it is often the uncertain, in-between spaces where genuine growth occurs.

**The** patterns of our lives reveal themselves slowly, like photographs developing in a darkroom. The choices we make, the people we encounter, the paths we abandon—each contributes to a larger picture we can only see clearly in retrospect. The present moment feels chaotic and directionless, yet the accumulated weight of our days eventually forms something resembling a story, even if we never intended to write one.

**Each** person carries a world within them, invisible to others yet entirely real. Each memory, however small, shapes the lens through which we view everything that follows. Each interaction leaves a trace, however faint, on both parties involved. To truly listen to another person is to acknowledge that each of us is navigating a complexity that can never be fully shared, only glimpsed and respected.

Together, these three ideas—the concession of *though*, the specificity of *the*, and the individuality of *each*—remind us that life resists simple summary. It is not a single truth but a mosaic of nuance, particularity, and quiet contradiction. Perhaps that is precisely why it remains worth exploring.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem about unrequited love using as many French loanwords/phrases as possible (like "cri de cœur," "fait accompli," "tour de force")
counterfactuals.output:
**Fait Accompli**

I saw you first—a *coup de foudre*, swift and true,
some *je ne sais quoi* drew my every thought to you.
Your *silhouette* against the café light
became at once my *raison d'être*, my delight.

I nursed a *penchant* growing wild and unrestrained,
a *tour de force* of longing, carefully sustained.
I wrote a *billet-doux* with trembling hand,
rehearsed each word like some half-broken band.

I begged a *rendezvous* beneath a paling moon,
you came, *ma belle*, but left me far too soon—
your practiced *savoir-faire*, your *chic* disdain,
looked past my heart to someone else's name.

Your answer came: a *fait accompli*, cold and plain,
no use for pleading, no encore, no refrain.
I'd made, perhaps, some foolish *faux pas* there—
mistook your kindness for a love laid bare.

Now *ennui* settles like a slow *malaise*,
I wander through the wreckage of those days.
Each *souvenir* a small, unwelcome guest,
each memory a wound I can't put to rest.

*Amour propre* wounded, pride in disarray,
I whisper *adieu* to what I couldn't say.
This is my *cri de cœur*, unanswered, thrown
into a silence that is yours alone.

*C'est la vie*, they murmur, with a Gallic shrug,
as if the heart's a wound one simply shrugs
away with reason, with love found elsewhere—
but *mon amour*, you were my only prayer.

So here's my *déjà vu* of hopes deferred,
my private *mirage* that never stirred
beyond my own reflection in your eyes—
*fait accompli*. My heart's own compromise.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you compose a witty, longing poem about pining after someone who doesn't reciprocate, packed with French expressions commonly used in English?
counterfactuals.output:
# Coup de Foudre, Unrequited

I saw you once—*coup de foudre*, they claim,
A thunderbolt struck, though you don't know my name.
I offered *carte blanche*, my heart's résumé—
You answered "*non, merci*" in your breezy way.

I sent the *RSVP* to my heart's *soirée*;
No answer arrived. *Quelle surprise*, per se.
This *je ne sais quoi* that keeps pulling me near
You wear like perfume you don't even hear.

*Au contraire*, I swear this ain't *déjà vu*—
though I've loved and lost, this time it was you.
*Entre nous*, I confess it's a bit of a *faux pas*,
loving someone who just shrugs and says "*bah*."

*C'est la vie*, I sigh, stirring bitter *café*,
scripting our future—a one-man *ballet*.
*Mon Dieu*, what a *raison d'être*, absurd and unheard,
A whole *tour de force* built on one unreturned word.

I lay my *amour-propre* out on a plate;
you *RSVP* silence—ah, *quelle fate*.
Still I raise "*à votre santé*" from afar—
*bon voyage* to my hopes, wherever they are.

You're the *crème de la crème*, *hors concours*, unattained,
while I'm the *cliché* fool, forever refrained.
*Encore, encore*, cries this heart, out of season,
knocking at doors closed for perfectly good reason.

So here's my *faux pas*, laid bare, *mon ami*—
this unrequited, *café*-fueled ennui.
*Au revoir* to my pride, *savoir-faire* be damned,
just a fool on one knee, *s'il vous plaît*-ing—unmanned.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a free-verse poem set around Memorial Drive about obsessive infatuation, incorporating French phrases like "mise en scène," "tête à tête," and "coup de grâce" for ironic effect.
counterfactuals.output:
**Memorial Drive, Repeating**

I park where the river bends
like an argument I keep losing,
engine ticking down to silence,
and call it *mise en scène*—
the streetlamp's amber wash,
the exact bench where you sat
telling me this was nothing,
this was just two people
talking near water.

I have memorized the traffic pattern
of your evenings. I know when the light
at the footbridge stutters
from walk to don't, and I am there,
always there, arranging my face
into someone who isn't waiting.

Call it a *tête-à-tête*, this monologue
I perform for the Charles,
for the geese who don't care,
for the runners who lap me
twice before I've finished
constructing your response
in a voice that sounds like you
but agrees with everything I want.

I used to think love was a door.
Now I know it's a rehearsal
that never opens to an audience,
just this same stretch of pavement,
same dying light, same
me, adjusting the blocking
of a scene you walked out of
in March.

Somewhere you are living
an ordinary Tuesday—
groceries, a phone call, sleep—
while I am still here
composing the *coup de grâce*,
some perfect, devastating thing
I'll say when I finally see you,
though I know, I know,
the mercy would be silence,
the mercy would be
walking home
the other way.

But I don't. I take the long route
past the boathouse, past
the place we stood not-quite-touching,
and call this fidelity,
call this passion,
when it is only
repetition
wearing a nicer coat,
only the same three chords
of wanting,
played each night
until the river takes them,
indifferent,
downstream,
gone.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a clever, melancholic love poem that uses French idioms as a recurring stylistic device, ending with a play on "reculer pour mieux sauter."
counterfactuals.output:
**Coup de Grâce**

We began, as always, with a bolt of lightning—
*coup de foudre*, you called it, laughing,
not knowing lightning only marks
what it means to burn down later.

For weeks I carried *le cafard*
in my chest like a stowaway cockroach,
some small dark thing of you
that scuttled each time your name was spoken.

You said I lived *dans la lune*,
too far in the moon, too distant,
as if loving you were not
the most lucid thing I'd ever done.

Some nights the *vague à l'âme* came—
that vagueness of the soul,
a fog too soft to have an edge,
too old for any idiom to fix.

I *broyais du noir* with both hands,
milled the black grain fine as flour,
baked it into a bread
I could never quite finish eating.

You poured water in your wine—
*mettre de l'eau dans son vin*—
until what we were
grew too thin for either of us to taste.

Still I called a cat a cat,
*appelé un chat un chat*,
said plainly: I love you—
and plainly, you were already leaving.

Now I stand at the edge of us,
one foot already in the after,
and if the French are right
that retreat is just a longer runway—

then let this be *reculer pour mieux sauter*—
not a step away from you, love,
but the small, aching distance
a heart needs to leap far enough to land.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.output:
**Coup de Foudre, One-Sided**

I felt the *coup de foudre* the night we met—
a thunderbolt, though you scarce looked my way;
my heart, an eager, naïve ingénue, set
the stage for our imagined *tête-à-tête*.

I came equipped with *savoir-faire* and *chic*,
rehearsed *bons mots* to make your eyebrows rise,
but every carefully-plotted *déjà vu*
dissolved beneath the boredom in your eyes.

I called it fate; you called it a *faux pas*—
my texts, it seems, were *une catastrophe*.
I sent a note that read, in bold: "*Voilà*,
my heart, entire, *à la carte*, and free."

You filed me swiftly in the *cul-de-sac*
of men who mean well but amount to naught,
while I composed, with tragic sense of chic,
this whole affair as one *avant-garde* thought.

My friends advise: "*Cherchez la dignité*,"
but dignity's a country I can't find;
I've built a *mise en scène*, a one-man play
where you're the star and I'm the wreck behind.

You are, I must confess, my *bête noire*—
my *raison d'être* wrapped in your disdain;
I've made a *papier-mâché* heart so far
it hardly notices the same old pain.

Still, *c'est la vie*—I'll bow, my sad *adieu*,
and call this *denouement* a kind of art.
*Touché*, dear stranger. I concede to you
the *coup de grâce* you dealt my foolish heart.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
